spec.title: PROP-073 — Shared source decisions and operation effects

SOURCE-EVIDENCE.title: Selected source facts and acquired provenance

p.SOURCE-EVIDENCE-LAW: One shared source-evidence model carries facts supplied by the existing resolver and acquisition owners. Preserve canonical origin and registry naming separately from the route actually used to acquire or read bytes; continuation locations and launcher origin are not package provenance. A commit, hosting or candidate reason is present only when observed or deterministically known from the relevant owned input; legacy missing evidence remains unknown and is never reconstructed from current registry settings. Source evidence is not package content identity, publisher authentication, a new source resolver or permission to execute. Do not expose credential material in source reports.

p.SOURCE-EVIDENCE-APPLICATIONS: Application plans, list and describe project the shared generated source evidence. A newly resolved source is separate from installed history. Durable application inventory and retained steps/import work preserve observations through supported update/replacement/rollback/import/resume paths, using strict versioned readers and compatible copied launchers. Fresh portable import records its actual acquisition; skipping an existing installation retains that installation's history. Legacy absent evidence remains unknown.

p.SOURCE-EVIDENCE-PROJECT-EVENTS: Real project install plan events carry the selected and acquired source observations through the existing installation observer, rather than reconstruct them from current registry settings. Their generated wire schema must match the actual producer shape and event timing. Application source-evidence support does not discharge this project event requirement or the separate read-only preview contract.

HOSTING-OBSERVATION.title: Derived hosting labels of recorded source addresses

p.HOSTING-OBSERVATION-LAW: One pure endpoint observation owner classifies the spelled host of supported remote addresses using deterministic parsing, without DNS, Git or SSH configuration, current registry settings or network probes. Exact recognized public repository hosts may yield hosting labels; custom, opaque, local or missing addresses do not acquire guessed labels. A derived report-only view distinguishes the selected origin URL from the independently recorded differing acquisition route. A missing route is not replaced with the canonical source, and store reuse is not a new contact. The same view accompanies existing project and global application source reports, with current authored source separate from installed history. Wire labels remain extensible strings; existing persisted SourceEvidence and closed inventory/work readers are unchanged. These are observations of recorded address spelling, not authenticated source identity, transport reachability, an actual-contact list or permission to fetch. Preference and exclusion require their own existing-owner admission and selection consumers.

HOSTING-OBSERVATION.p: Initial recognized public repository hosts: exact normalized github.com maps to github; gitverse.ru maps to gitverse. Verified 2026-11-07 against [GitHub remote documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/git-basics/about-remote-repositories) and [GitVerse clone documentation](https://gitverse.ru/docs/collaborative/repositories/guides/repository-workflow/clone-repository). This is not a claim about all service domains or self-hosted installations.

SOURCE-POLICY.title: Effective registry constraints and contact policy

p.SOURCE-POLICY-LAW: Registry pins constrain requirement edges against the operation's effective project/user registry catalog; unknown names and incompatible incoming pins refuse without silent fallback. They do not implicitly authorize new registries declared by a dependency. Hosting preference ranks equivalent candidates at a fixed selected version, with configured registry order as tie-breaker; absent policy preserves existing selection semantics. Hosting exclusion governs actual managed destinations before discovery or fetch, including redirect, remap, mirror and fallback. A presentation label cannot override destination checks. Unsupported opaque routes cannot be claimed to satisfy a no-contact guarantee. Candidate reports distinguish observed, excluded and not-probed states; lack of contact is not evidence of remote absence or exclusive availability.

LOCKED-SOURCE.title: Locked source authority versus new registry selection

p.LOCKED-SOURCE-LAW: Registry configuration selects new package sources and index discovery. A package already present in the held lock resolves and acquires from its locked source and revision/content constraints; current registry edits cannot retarget it. Missing cached content requires the locked source, and failure must not silently choose a current registry or mirror. Verified no-contact reuse is permitted without claiming a new acquisition. Ordinary install, reinstall or cache repair does not authorize source reselection. An unchanged authoritative selection preserves the original shared lock bytes, including generation metadata; developer credentials, local paths and transport preferences do not rewrite shared source identity. Optional provenance reports remain reports, not hidden resolution authority. Deliberate update or relock is a distinct operation contract. Existing local-change protection and checked publication/recovery remain in force.

LOCKED-SOURCE.p: Owner decision 2026-11-08 supersedes automatic HTTPS/SSH migration of already locked packages after registry.toml changes. This rule is planned; current online registry walking and unconditional lock generation timestamps still require implementation. Ordinary user SSH setup must be connected through the existing source owners for new SSH registries and locked SSH sources, without a second resolver.

HTTP-ADMISSION.title: Bounded HTTP-only admission capability

p.HTTP-ADMISSION-LAW: An explicit immutable HTTP-only binding is installed before a constrained client or resolver can probe or request. It checks the actual constructed initial URL and every redirect/retry destination before contact, preserving typed refusal independently of absence, transport, authentication and malformed data. A refusal consumes no retries and cannot be laundered into an optimization decline or ungated native fallback. Bound pools and anonymous backend clones retain the same binding. The bounded client owns its redirects and retries, has no ambient proxy or automatic transport replay, and confines credentials to the authorized origin; cross-origin stripping is permanent within a chain. Invalid redirect, finite-hop exhaustion, unsupported scheme and HTTPS downgrade refuse before the next request. Native subprocess paths under this HTTP-only capability refuse before spawn; positive admitted HTTP paths remain functional. Absence of binding preserves incumbent behavior. This internal capability is not an exposed whole-operation hosting exclusion setting, a DNS/IP egress sandbox or a substitute for the remaining admitted Git/submodule and route-choice implementation. Diagnostic endpoints do not expose credentials or query data.

HTTP-ADMISSION.p: Denied-host and hosting keys share pure host normalization, including a single terminal DNS root dot and normalized IP/IDNA spellings; malformed empty-label authorities refuse. DNS root-dot equivalence does not broaden HTTP credential-origin equality: redirect credentials still use the existing exact URL scheme/host/effective-port boundary. Original source URLs remain unchanged.

p.NATIVE-PREPARATION-LAW: A separate native preparation capability shares the immutable denied-host policy without relaxing the accepted HTTP-only native refusal. Its caller explicitly supplies a trusted Git executable/helper installation and TLS trust inputs; these are not package-supplied flags or claims of executable authentication. Supported HTTPS object acquisition and bounded metadata operations run in operation-owned transport contexts with captured endpoints, controlled configuration/environment and origin-scoped ephemeral credentials. They do not inherit ambient transport rewrites, helpers, proxies, hooks or recursive acquisition. Warm effective endpoints must be captured with their supported configuration meaning or refused before contact; unexamined global/include semantics are not assumed empty and recorded A is not silently substituted for effective B. Source identities, selected commit/object witnesses and existing guarded apply/recovery authority remain intact. Unbound behavior is unchanged. Unsupported publication, SSH, transforms, lazy object fetch, redirects or submodule traversal remain explicit capability boundaries until separately proved and implemented; universal native refusal is not the final source-exclusion feature.

NATIVE-MATERIALISATION.title: Captured native staging and checked publication

p.NATIVE-MATERIALISATION-LAW: Supported native materialisation captures the selected Git configuration/attribute meanings, effective and recorded origins, retained source objects and old slot witnesses without executing uncontrolled helpers or assuming unexamined context empty. It stages byte-equivalent supported payload transformations in an owned context; unsupported active transforms/layouts or missing ownership refuse before caller metadata or slot publication. Actual fresh and warm planning must carry the prepared result without forcing ordinary copy packages into in-place mode or treating policy refusal as a non-applicable route. Workspace owns neutral exact-identity placement and the existing undo log; registry owns source bytes and revalidation, with no reverse dependency or second transaction framework. Every deferred checked native slot and related gitignore effect is captured before replacement, then retained through final metadata success. Unknown post-publication edits or foreign replacements are preserved with explicit rollback conflict and retained old backup, not silently attributed to this operation. Immediate lifecycle deletion must not bypass checked ownership. This is cooperative guarded recovery, not hostile-race CAS or arbitrary external-script rollback. Legacy hook/park semantics remain unless a specific shared correction is independently proved. N2 staging alone does not complete local publication, and N3/N4 or public exclusion are not inferred from it.

NATIVE-MATERIALISATION.p: The initial checked materialisation profile is Unix-only, qualified on Linux with Git 2.53.0. Supported built-in text/EOL conversion is captured; active external filters, ident/working-tree-encoding, unsupported repository layouts and unqualified transport meanings refuse explicitly. Fresh conditional includes refuse when their final checkout context cannot be reproduced. A native plan may include ordinary cache-backed packages; mixing native placements with legacy deferred in-place mutations refuses before caller writes because that legacy path lacks shared checked rollback. SSH and recursive/redirect routes are qualified separately by NATIVE-SSH and NATIVE-ROUTES below; public policy settings remain separate work.

p.NATIVE-SSH-LAW: A native SSH capability uses an explicitly trusted OpenSSH installation, exact host/user/port, captured known-host trust and either a captured private key or an explicitly selected agent socket. Actual requests check normalized denied-host policy before contact while credential and trust selection retains exact endpoint identity. Strict host-key verification, noninteractive authentication and disabled forwarding remain mandatory. No ambient SSH aliases, proxy commands, local commands or credential providers execute. The explicit-direct profile is caller-selected transport authority for fresh and warm operations; it is not inferred from a recorded origin and does not claim equivalence to historical SSH configuration. Existing Git-origin and source witnesses still recheck. Metadata observation and actual credential-use admission are distinct. Immutable per-registry bindings allow anonymous HTTPS reads, permit HTTPS Basic/token credentials only for TokenEnv, and permit SSH key/agent use only for Ssh; anonymous/public binding and rebinding cannot acquire broader credential authority. Direct backend use retains its separately explicit profile authority. Failures are typed and redacted without laundering policy or trust refusal into absence or an ungated fallback. Actual authenticated acquisition, fresh/warm installation, denied-route and wrong-key controls are required before acceptance; recipe-only proof is insufficient. Recursive routes are qualified separately by NATIVE-ROUTES; public source-policy settings remain separate work.

SSH-CONFIG-CAPTURE.title: Ordinary user SSH inputs for an already selected source

p.SSH-CONFIG-CAPTURE-LAW: The source owner chooses the address first: current registry for new packages, locked source for locked packages. User SSH configuration supplies authentication, trust and explicitly captured endpoint meaning for that address; it cannot substitute the current registry for a locked source. A captured-config profile is distinct from explicit-direct authority. Selected OpenSSH may evaluate only an audited frozen configuration closure: unexamined includes, executable match conditions and unsupported active routing cannot execute or contact a host during discovery. Supported ordinary Host/include precedence, URL overrides, ordered identity files together with the permitted agent, IdentitiesOnly and known-host selection retain their meaning. Effective destinations are admitted before contact. Missing trust or credentials and unsupported active configuration produce explicit redacted failures, never an alternate transport. Existing keys and agent setup are reused without writing private keys into Vibe settings. Captured input witnesses are checked before use; caller publication retains existing checked recovery. Actual isolated authentication and configuration-parity tests are required; parser output alone is not proof of useful SSH integration.

SSH-CONFIG-CAPTURE.p: The internal captured-profile API is qualified on Linux/OpenSSH 10.2/Git 2.53 with real authentication, Include/default/key/agent parity, encrypted-key agent use, effective-host exclusion before identity/trust work, input/permission drift and selected algorithm controls. Unsupported active proxy/provider/certificate/revocation, relative identity/trust paths, dynamic Include tokens and recursive globs refuse explicitly. This is not full interactive OpenSSH equivalence. Ordinary CLI/global profile construction and declaration/locked-source integration remain planned; internal profile tests do not establish those user-facing flows.

Registry authentication declarations must retain omission separately from explicit none before transport-aware lowering. Existing explicit credential ceilings remain intact. Captured SSH support, declaration compatibility and real shared CLI/global integration are distinct work within the same user-facing feature; none is accepted merely because a helper type or parser exists.

NATIVE-ROUTES.title: Admitted alternatives, relocation and recursive Git sources

p.NATIVE-ROUTES-LAW: Source-selection owners may skip a concretely excluded route and try independently admitted alternatives without converting lower-level refusal into absence or an ungated fallback. The actual serving route is retained across lookup, redirect-marker reads and acquisition, separately from canonical source identity. Package redirects use the target owner's bound backend and credential authority. Initial HTTPS relocation follows the normal Git initial-request model through the bounded HTTP owner, preserves sticky cross-origin credential stripping and validated endpoint meaning, and leaves opaque native auto-follow disabled. Captured native PEM trust may be reused; bundled HTTP roots must never silently stand in for the selected Git installation's system trust, so that mode requires separately explicit HTTP discovery trust while direct native System requests remain supported. Every recursive child is selected from retained parent gitlink and module data, admitted before contact and acquired at its exact object identity. Original module URLs, selected raw URLs and warm recorded origins must be validated before rewriting can conceal unsupported URL credentials in derived repository metadata. Malformed authority-bearing URL input refuses rather than becoming an opaque rewrite alias; ordinary SSH usernames and supported relative/SCP addresses retain their meaning. Immutable authored Git objects are not rewritten to erase their input. Safe unique mount paths, captured warm overrides and explicit credential ceilings remain; missing, corrupt, unsafe or unqualified children refuse before caller publication. Parent and complete child trees stage together and publish through the existing checked workspace undo, with foreign-state conflict preservation. Allowed-route and authenticated recursive successes, relative-URL parity, denied-descendant zero-contact and whole-tree recovery require actual execution before acceptance. Public preference/exclusion settings are separate work.

NATIVE-ROUTES.p: Qualified on Linux with Git 2.53 and OpenSSH 10.2 through explicit native profiles. Actual tests cover allowed mirrors with denied-primary zero contact, pinned package redirects with independent target credentials, initial HTTPS relocation, exact nested gitlinks, mixed SSH/HTTPS/SSH profiles, fresh/warm embedded and managed absorbed layouts, and checked whole-tree recovery. Ordinary unbound source refresh semantics remain preserved. Prepared in-place actual-route evidence reaches the existing report-only provenance sidecar while canonical lock source stays unchanged. This completes the internal native route capability; ordinary user SSH-configuration capture, public registry transport integration and LOCKED-SOURCE-LAW remain planned, not implied by injected-profile proofs.

p.OPERATION-EFFECTS-LAW: Operation planning separates source resolution, acquisition effects and product publication. A project preview leaves the project, user HOME and persistent caches unchanged. The owner permits a separately owned temporary scratch directory for metadata acquisition, with mandatory cleanup after success, failure and cancellation. Existing acquisition may be reused only through an explicit scratch-bound effect contract; ordinary cache/config publication, hooks and wrapper-side application/remap/boot effects must not leak into preview. Reading verified existing content is allowed without refreshing it in place. Unsupported metadata access is reported explicitly rather than fabricated as a complete plan. Apply uses captured decisions or reports/replans drift rather than promising a mutable ref is unchanged. Cancellation requests and stopped outcomes are distinct. Before product publication, cooperative cancellation preserves project state; during owned local publication use existing guarded recovery. Completed or unknown external effects and rollback conflicts are reported truthfully, never labeled successful restoration. Reuse lifecycle and progress owners rather than create a parallel orchestrator. Logical successful-write counters are distinct from received bytes, retained file size and physical disk I/O.
